This dataset is extracted from the DeepSeaSpy database (https://www.deepseaspy.com/)
Annotations of the images are made by citizen, and are in 3 different formats depending on the species labeled : Points, Lines and Polygons.

# Dataset description
In this section, you will find the description of the columns of the 3 available datasets :
        - Raw dataset, not modified from the DeepSeaSpy database.
        - Cleaned dataset, the specification of the cleaning can be found further in the readme.
        - Expert dataset, labeled by an expert.

For each dataset, two columns are in common :
name_img : Name of the labeled image. The first element is the site where the picture was taken (MOMAR for the Azores, or TEMPO for Juan de Fuca). Then, the date and the time when the picture was taken. This information can also be found in the image file name, and on the top left of the images.
name_sp : Name of the species labeled.

## Raw dataset
x1 : The x coordinate of the first point (for lines and points)
y1 : The y coordinate of the first point (for lines and points)
x2 : The x coordinate of the second point (for lines)
y2 : The y coordinate of the second point (for lines)
length : The length of the line (for lines)
middle_x : The x coordinate of the middle of the line (for lines)
middle_y : The y coordinate of the middle of the line (for lines)
polygon_values : The coordinates of the polygon (for polygons)

## Cleaned dataset
xmin : The minimal x coordinate of the label bounding box.
xmax : The maximum x coordinate of the label bounding box.
ymin : The minimal y coordinate of the label bounding box.
ymax : The maximum y coordinate of the label bounding box.
length : The length of the diagonal of the bounding box.
occurences : The number of overlapping bounding boxes unified to create the row.

## Expert dataset
xmin : The minimal x coordinate of the label bounding box.
xmax : The maximum x coordinate of the label bounding box.
ymin : The minimal y coordinate of the label bounding box.
ymax : The maximum y coordinate of the label bounding box.
length : The length of the diagonal of the bounding box.

# Dataset cleaning
This section is dedicated to explain how we got the cleaned dataset from the raw one. The cleaning of the dataset was done using the pipeline provided in the github repository : https://github.com/ai4os-hub/deep-species-detection

## Format conversion
There is a non avoidable data imbalance in the dataset depending on the citizens labeling preferences, which is heavily leaning toward species that are the easiest to identify. We selected only 2 species from the 2 different observation sites for this cleaned dataset (Buccinidae and Bythograeidae). Those two are the most represented in each sites, and best annotated by citizens.

First, we converted the original Deep Sea Spy annotation format to a regular bounding box format (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax). Deep Sea Spy annotations range from :
    - Lines, defined by 2 points.
    - Points, defined by a single point.
    - Polygons, defined by multiple points in json format.

For the conversion of lines, we added a correction based on the angle of the line with the x axis. This makes sure the conversion of the lines would not create unusable rectangle bounding boxes. The margin we used to determine if the angle of the line is considered problematic is 18°. The correction is the expansion of the bounding box, on either the x coordinates (if the line is near 180° of the x axis) or y coordinates (if the line is near 90° of the x axis). The correction is half of the length of the line.
A padding of 25 pixels was added to the annotation of Bythograeidae, because Deep Sea Spy required an annotation of the cephalothorax and not the whole crab. The padding allows a clear visualization of the whole crab for the YoloV8 model training, thus improving the model performances.

## Unification of bounding boxes
The redundancy of information was used as a way to cross validate the presence of an animal. This cleaning is done in 2 steps. First, the pipeline unifies bounding boxes based on an IoU threshold : bounding boxes that have an IoU of 0.6 or higher with any other bounding box are kept. The others are discarded. Then, a measure of the minimal IoU between bounding boxes that are still overlapping is done. If they are of 0.4 or higher, they are unified in the final dataset. Other unified bounding boxes from the first step, that were not overlapping another one for the second step, were kept.

# YoloV8 training
Two models (YOLOv8n - architecture nano) were trained on the cleaned dataset. Each species was trained on a separate model, as they are from different observation sites(bythograeidae.pt, buccinidae.pt). 
For the training on Buccinidae, expert annotations were used as validation for the training on citizen annotations. The best model has a precision/recall of 0.6, but low confidence on its detections (mAP50-95 at 0.15 vs mAP50 at 0.5, meaning there is a higher precision with lower confidence).
For the training on Bythograeidae, no expert annotations were available for the validation of the training on citizen annotations, so a part of the citizen dataset was used as validation. The best model has a precision/recall of 0.4, and like the Buccinidae model, a low confidence in its detections (mAP50-95 at 0.1 vs mAP50 at 0.3, meaning there is a higher precision with lower confidence).
The models were trained on 150 epochs, batch size of 16. No fine tuning of hyperparameter was done.
